text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed table rows get squished on very narrow widths when the sidebar is collapsed. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.dev/ux/squish-iphone-se.png
maria: Hmm can you repro on iPhone SE? Is this with compact rows enabled?
alex: Yes iPhone SE, compact rows on. The action column (three-dots) moves to next line and causes the whole row to wrap, looks off.
jamie: Noted. Could be two ways: 1) hide non-essential columns under 360px, or 2) surface a tiny "minimap" affordance to open details for the row.
alex: By "minimap" you mean a small pill / icon at the start of the row that opens a compact flyout?
maria: Exactly. I sketched a variant where we collapse secondary columns and replace them with a 32px affordance that opens a stacked detail panel. Important: keyboard focus target and screenreader label.
maria: Prototype CSS snippet: ```css
@media (max-width: 380px) {
  .table-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 44px; gap: 8px; }
  .action-col { min-width: 44px; text-align: right; }
}
```
jamie: I like the idea but worried about discoverability. If it's hidden behind an icon labeled "Details" users might miss it. Maybe the affordance should be a labelled pill "Show details" instead of just an ellipsis. Accessibility favours explicit copy.
alex: Good point — copy tweak: "Show details" vs "More" — which reads clearer on small screens?
sam: Quick hallway test: showed both to 12 people. "Show details" had faster success rate (67%) vs "More" (48%). People preferred explicit language. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maria: I'll update mock to use "Show details" and add aria-expanded="false" on the trigger. Also will ensure expanded panel has role="dialog" for easier discoverability.
jamie: Also: when panel opens, trap focus, and return focus to the trigger on close. Add a visually hidden close button for SR users.
alex: Another nit — when the sidebar is collapsed and table horizontally scrolls, the sticky headers jump. Can we avoid layout shift by reserving the action column width?
maria: We can reserve the 44px gap via CSS and enable `contain: layout` on the table row to reduce reflow. Need to validate on Android smaller webviews, too.
js: (react-dev-bot) linked issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/2845 referencing mobile table redesign
design-bot: New design PR opened — https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2845 — includes mocks, accessibility checklist, and a small playbook for rollout behind feature flag `compact_table_minimap`.
alex: Good — shall we canary this behind the feature flag and run a quick telemetry test for click-through on the pill?
maria: Yes, canary first. I'll add telemetry to the trigger (`ui.table.compact_minimap.opened`) and a variant for copy A/B ("Show details" vs "Details").
jamie: Add QA checklist: iPhone SE Safari, Pixel 4 Chrome, VoiceOver + TalkBack, keyboard-only flow. Also test with long labels in the first column — ensure ellipsis and tooltip show on hover/focus.
alex: Awesome. Thanks team — I'll add a note to the release checklist and link the canary experiment. :thumbsup:
